transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi, yes, thank you. Um, well, what brings me in is... it's about work. I teach preschool, and the second I spot balloons at school—even if they're all the way across the hallway—my chest just completely tightens up. I freeze for a moment before I can even think clearly about what I’m actually supposed to be doing. 

Which is really hard, because, you know, they always have them for birthdays. Like last Tuesday, it was little Mason's birthday, and his mom brought in these huge ones. She’s a baker, actually, so she also brought these incredible cupcakes with little fondant dinosaurs on them. They were so cute, and honestly, the frosting was amazing, way better than the store-bought kind we usually get. I actually asked her for the recipe, but she said it's a family secret, which I get, but still. I tried making a buttercream last Thanksgiving and it completely separated on me. 

Um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the freezing. Yeah, I just... I lock up entirely when I see them.
Is your reaction limited to balloons, or do you experience similar feelings of tightness and freezing with other objects or situations as well?

Um, no, it's really just the balloons. Like, I know a balloon in the classroom is probably just a decoration, you know? But when I see one stretched so tight, or just bobbing around near the children... it feels like it could burst right in my face. I get scared in a way that seems way, way bigger than the situation. 

It's not like I'm afraid of other things popping, either. Like bubble wrap! I'm completely fine with bubble wrap. The kids actually love it—we use it for sensory play all the time. Just last week we painted some with yellow tempera paint and pressed it onto construction paper to make it look like corn on the cob for our farm unit. The farm unit is always my absolute favorite to teach. We usually do a field trip to Miller's Farm, but they raised their group rates this year so the PTA said we couldn't go. Which is such a shame because they have this amazing petting zoo with the sweetest baby goats. I really wanted a pygmy goat growing up, but my dad was strictly a "dogs only" kind of guy. We had a Golden Retriever named Buster who used to dig up all my mom's hydrangeas... 

But anyway, yeah, bubble wrap and other stuff like that is totally fine. It's literally just the balloons.
